correctness.rationale: The periodized line kernel solves the cycle resolvent recurrence; restriction to the two sites has eigenforms g₀±g_d, positive and strictly decreasing via the squared-resolvent derivative. The plus form diverges at 2 and the minus form has edge limit d(N−d)/(2N) from the product of hyperbolic sines. Each channel contributes at most one level; since g_d>0 the roots are distinct and each is simple. Positivity excludes levels below −2. At E=2, summing the eigen-equation forces opposite defect values; interpolation on each arc gives the defect equation V=2/d+2/(N−d), including d=1 and N=3. With r_N=min(d_N,N−d_N)/N, the strictly decreasing scaled threshold on (0,1/2] implies the exact critical count r_N>ρ and the edge condition r_N=ρ; at ρ=1/2 this denies a second strictly above-edge level for every N. The finite secular functions converge on compact positive intervals. Their analytic, unbounded, nondecreasing limits are strictly increasing; bracketing gives all asserted positive root limits. At the critical coupling the minus function is strictly larger than λ at any fixed positive y, so any existing minus roots have y_N→0, giving zero scaled shift. The tanh/coth specialization follows directly by half-angle identities.
residual_risks: The recorded 40 numerical assertions are frozen author evidence, not independently executed. They check selected cycles/couplings, not the equality-sequence theorem; the independent check there is analytic. No scaling at limiting fraction zero is claimed.

value.rationale: Two equal sites on a periodic nearest-neighbour lattice form a canonical bound-state problem. An exact all-N count and edge criterion distinguish the always-present level from the onset of a second one, with explicit dependence on separation. Connecting these lattice levels to the continuum functions and resolving the finite separations at critical scaling gives more information than computing a particular parameter slice or restating the continuum determinant.
residual_risks: The contribution is a specific lattice theorem, not a new general resolvent technique or a claim for interactions beyond the stated model.
